pages.text: Sylvite, KCl, is salt's potassium twin, colourless when pure and red in the Saskatchewan mines, where a dust of hematite stains it. It is the last salt to crystallise as a sea dries up, so it lies in seams in the evaporite beds with the halite. Mined with its halite, it is sylvinite.
pages.title: Sylvite

pages.text: Potassium chloride dissolves far better hot than cold and salt hardly better at all, so the hot leach parts them, as the Carlsbad and Saskatchewan mills do: two raw sylvite and 500 mB of water, heated, give two potash, the muriate of potash farmers buy, and a salt. Nearly all potash is fertiliser.
pages.title: Muriate of potash

pages.text: Here it is also the bath lithium is electrolysed in and the potassium the tantalum salt is crystallised with.
Sources: USGS, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025, Potash; Garrett, Potash: Deposits, Processing, Properties and Uses (Chapman & Hall, 1996).
